title: He ruled for 30 days…
paragraphs:
He ruled for 30 days…
—and lost everything.
King Shallum didn’t wait his turn. He didn’t seek God. He didn’t inherit the throne.
And for a moment… it worked.
The crown fit. The seat was his. The power felt real.
But the silence of God was louder than the cheers of men.
And that’s where the story turns.

Because 2 Kings 15 tells us something chilling without saying much at all: Shallum assassinated Zechariah, seized the throne, and reigned in Samaria for one month before Menahem struck him down and took his place.
That’s all sin could sustain him.
We don’t talk about this kind of failure.
The kind that looks like success at first.

The kind where you finally get what you wanted…
—and realize God was never in it.
Because here’s the truth we avoid:
Not everything you achieve is something God approved.
And some of us are living in “one-month victories.”
Doors we kicked open instead of prayed over.
We don’t say it out loud…
Because it’s easier to sit on a stolen throne than to admit we never belonged there.
What are you holding onto that you had to compromise to get?
What did you say “yes” to… that God never anointed?
Here’s the hidden struggle nobody posts about:
So we created our own version of “blessing.”
And like Shallum, we call it destiny.
But Scripture cuts through the illusion.
James 3:16 says where jealousy and selfish ambition exist, there will be disorder and every vile practice.
Selfish ambition doesn’t just corrupt outcomes.
Shallum didn’t just lose a kingdom.
Because this is where it gets uncomfortable.

You can be surrounded by spiritual language…
and still be driven by flesh.

You can say “God opened this door”…
when you were the one who broke the lock.
God will never bless what you had to sin to build.
Not because He is against you.
But because He loves you too much to let your soul be fed by something that will eventually destroy you.
Proverbs 10:22 says the blessing of the Lord makes rich, and He adds no sorrow with it.
If it comes with hidden anxiety, constant fear of exposure, and a quiet distance from God…
If God removed it today, would you feel relief… or panic?
Because that answer reveals what’s really ruling you.
Shallum had a crown on his head…
He had power in his hands…
And when Menahem came, it was over.
Because when God is not sustaining what you’re holding, it will not last.
Some scholars interpret Shallum’s rapid downfall as part of God’s judgment on a long line of corrupt kings in Israel—a cycle of violence producing more violence.
That’s the part nobody talks about.
You won’t just lose what you built.
And they won’t need to fight hard.
Because what isn’t rooted in God has no foundation to stand on.
But here’s where grace steps in.
Because this isn’t just Shallum’s story.
Romans 3:23 says all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.
But verse 24 doesn’t leave us there—it says we are justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.
That’s the turning point Shallum never took.
Because the real tragedy is not that he died.
It’s that there’s no record he ever turned.
And that’s the danger for us.
You cannot recover from pride that refuses correction.
Philippians 2 says He humbled Himself, becoming obedient to death—even death on a cross.
While Shallum shed blood to gain power…
Jesus shed His own blood to save sinners.
You don’t have to hold onto what you forced.
You don’t have to pretend anymore.
You don’t have to keep sitting on something that’s draining your soul.
Because when you surrender to Jesus, you don’t lose everything.
2 Corinthians 5:17 says if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.
Not a rebranded version of your old ambition.
Where did you take what God never gave?
Where are you still holding on… because you’re afraid of what happens if you let go?
And receive grace that doesn’t expire in 30 days.
If this hit something deep in you, don’t ignore it.
There’s more truth coming that will confront, heal, and restore what pride tried to protect.
Because God is not just calling you out.
And the next message might be the one you didn’t know you needed.
